name: preterm_28wk
description: Literature reference values for a preterm neonate born at 28 weeks (~1 kg) at ~72 h postnatal age, stable on nasal CPAP 6 cmH2O with FiO2 0.25, a small restrictive left-to-right PDA (~1 mm), untransfused, delayed cord clamping, trophic feeds + PN, caffeine, humidified incubator. Grades: A = 27-30 wk infants on day 2-4, B = wider GA band / other day / figure readout / guideline, C = textbook / extrapolation / derived.
state: stable on nCPAP 6, FiO2 0.25, small restrictive L->R PDA, PFO, untransfused (delayed clamping), trophic feeds + PN, caffeine, incubator ~35 degC / 70 % RH

variables.label: Heart rate
variables.notes: Deshpande 160 (135-186) at 54 h, 25.9 wk; Bischoff 155-163 (25.5 wk, day 0-4). Groves MRI 142 +/- 17 was asleep and ~day 9. A 28-wk infant sits a few bpm below the 25-26 wk cohorts.

variables.label: Systolic BP
variables.notes: Elsayed Table 4, 28 wk D3 (P5/P25/P50/P75/P95 43/48/54/59/64), UAC, n=63 at 28 wk. Cuff cross-check: van Zadelhoff calculator GA 28+0 PNA 72 h 59.1 (46.8-73.5).

variables.label: Mean arterial pressure
variables.notes: Elsayed 28 wk D3 P5/P25/P50/P75/P95 30/34/39/43/47; 83 % of day-3 time between P25 and P75. Cuff reads ~4 mmHg higher (van Zadelhoff 43.4). The user's clinical 45/25 (MAP ~32) is low-normal, about P5-P10.

variables.label: Pulse pressure
variables.notes: Derived from the Elsayed medians.

variables.label: Central venous pressure
variables.notes: Trevor Inglis 2007 (27 wk, 940 g, UVC, days 1-4, mostly ventilated) median 4.9 (IQR 4.4-6.1); Choi 2015 VLBW 3.5 +/- 2.2 steady day 1-7. CPAP lowers venous return little at 6 cmH2O.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, systolic
variables.notes: Derived: RV/systemic systolic pressure ratio 0.55 (user's choice; Skinner 1992 at 37-72 h: 0.44 healthy preterm, 0.72 HMD) x SBP 54 ~ 30. Ratio grade B, mmHg grade C.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, mean
variables.notes: Derived from pap_s with the Chemla relation (0.61 x sPAP + 2); extrapolation.

variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure, diastolic
variables.notes: Constraint, not a measurement: pure left-to-right flow through a restrictive duct needs PA pressure below aortic pressure through the whole cycle, so PA diastolic < aortic diastolic (~29). Skinner 1991: pure high-velocity L->R ductal flow went with a pressure ratio 0.49-0.66.

variables.label: LV end-diastolic volume
variables.notes: Groves MRI 2.51 +/- 0.40 (LLN 1.8), no GA effect, at SV 1.73 / HR 142. Scaled to the echo-anchored SV 1.4 at EF ~65 % (user decision: echo SV anchor).

variables.label: LV stroke volume
variables.notes: User decision: echo SV anchor. LVO/HR: Deshpande 1.23, Bischoff 1.07, Kluckow-implied ~1.5; MRI 1.73 (older, HR 142) is the upper bracket.

variables.label: LV ejection fraction
variables.notes: Groves MRI 69 +/- 5.7 (LLN 58), no GA effect. 3D echo reads lower (Toyoshima LVEF 44 % in duct-closed controls on day 14) - method dependent.

variables.label: RV end-diastolic volume
variables.notes: No preterm first-week RV volumes exist (Groves did not report RV). Derived from RV SV and EF ~50 %.

variables.label: RV end-systolic volume
variables.notes: Derived.

variables.label: RV ejection fraction
variables.notes: 3D echo RVEF 52 % (Toyoshima, day 14 controls). Echo FAC 26-35 % at 24-72 h (Levy 2015) is a different index.

variables.label: RV fractional area change
variables.notes: Levy 2015, 23-28 wk, 24-72 h: FAC ~26 +/- 4 %, stable through 72 h; James 2016 day-1 31 %. Not a model output (reference only).

variables.label: TAPSE
variables.notes: Koestenberger 2011 linear 0.44 cm at 26 wk to 1.03 at 41 wk, interpolated to 28 wk. Reference only.

variables.label: Left ventricular output
variables.notes: Day-3 echo: Deshpande 197 at 54 h; Bischoff no-PDA 170 (day 1) vs hsPDA 250; Kluckow-implied ~230 at 48 h; outputs rise day 1 -> 4 (Evans 1996). MRI 222 (Groves, day ~10) and Sloot 2010 day 7 (296) are upper brackets. Must satisfy LVO = SVC + DAo + ductal shunt (+ coronaries).

variables.label: Right ventricular output
variables.notes: Deshpande 194; Bischoff 161-170; MRI 219. RVO = systemic venous return + left-to-right atrial shunt.

variables.label: LVO/RVO ratio
variables.notes: Defines 'haemodynamically insignificant' PDA: Bischoff median 0.98 (no PDA) vs 1.44 (hsPDA). Equals (Qs + PDA) / (Qs + FO).

variables.label: SVC flow
variables.notes: User decision: anchored on MRI, then lowered from 95 to 85 so the flows close with LVO 215 and a PDA shunt. Kluckow 86 at 48 h (<30 wk); Deshpande 85 at 54 h; Groves MRI 95 +/- 27; Bischoff 73 (modified) / 108 (traditional). Echo SVC reads ~14 below MRI with wide scatter (Ficial 2013).

variables.label: Descending aorta flow
variables.notes: Groves MRI 126 +/- 32 (duct closed). Lowered to 110 so LVO = SVC + DAo + duct closes (Broadhouse 2013). Split: SMA 25 + coeliac 20 + kidneys 10 + rest ~55.

variables.label: Cerebral blood flow
variables.notes: ~18 mL/100 g/min x brain ~155 g (15-16 % of body weight). Greisen 1986 xenon, 28-33 wk week 1: CPAP 21.3 +/- 12.0, no RDS 19.8 +/- 5.3 mL/100 g/min. Pereira 2021 carotid Doppler day 3 (<29 wk) 14 mL/kg/min one side -> ~28 total. Brain gets ~30 % of SVC flow, not the often-quoted 80 %. CBF rises day 1 -> 3. Cerebral rSO2 ~65-70 % on day 3 (Alderliesten 2016).

variables.label: Intestinal (SMA) flow
variables.notes: State: trophic feeds + PN, between feeds. van Bel 1990 Doppler 43 +/- 13 (mixed GA; treated as an upper estimate). Velocity rises day 1 -> 3; CPAP and PN blunt the rise; post-feed rise ~80 %.

variables.label: Renal blood flow
variables.notes: User decision: lowered from 30. Visser 1992 Doppler (16 % of CO, ~42 mL/kg/min) treated as an overestimate. Newborn kidneys get ~3-6 % of CO; with GFR ~0.5 mL/min/kg this gives a filtration fraction of ~8 %.

variables.label: Coeliac (liver + spleen) flow
variables.notes: El-Khuffash 2008 controls (28.7 wk, 1110 g, day 3): coeliac flow/LVO mostly > 0.10, i.e. > ~21 at LVO 215. Liver is mostly portal-fed on day 3.

variables.label: Ductal shunt flow (L->R)
variables.notes: Small restrictive L->R duct. From LVO - RVO + FO: 215 - 195 + ~5. Must stay L->R all cycle.

variables.label: Ductal diameter
variables.notes: Deshpande 50 % patent at 54 h, median 1.12 mm; Bischoff hsPDA threshold >= 1.5 mm/kg (hsPDA mean 2.1 mm).

variables.label: Foramen ovale shunt (L->R)
variables.notes: Atrial communication in 93-100 % (Bischoff), mostly L->R with a small duct. No volume data.

variables.label: Respiratory rate
variables.notes: Welty 2018 (29.6 wk, 44 h, bubble CPAP 5-8) 67 +/- 20; Liew 2020 nCPAP 6 66 +/- 17 (older); Dimitriou 72-80 in week 1.

variables.label: Tidal volume
variables.notes: User decision: non-invasive (no mask) convention, as for term. Liew nCPAP 6: 4.7 +/- 2.1 (EIP); mask/pneumotach studies read ~15 % higher (5.4-6.7). Caffeine assumed (+~30 % Vt, Kraaijenga).

variables.label: Minute ventilation
variables.notes: Liew nCPAP 6: 315 +/- 176.

variables.label: Inspiratory time fraction (Ti/Ttot)
variables.notes: Reiterer Ti 0.36 s; Dimitriou I:E 0.67-0.77 -> Ti/Ttot 0.40-0.44 (derived). Ti ~0.35 s at RR 62.

variables.label: Respiratory system compliance
variables.notes: Absolute value at 1 kg. Lungs 0.8 mL/cmH2O/kg (user: middle of acute 0.45 and recovering 1.0-1.2) in series with chest wall ~5 /kg (Gerhardt 1980: 6.4 /kg) -> 0.69.

variables.label: Lung compliance (both lungs)
variables.notes: Bhutani 1988 0.44 /kg acute ventilated RDS; Cunningham ~0.8 /kg (derived); Reiterer 1.16 absolute recovering; surfactant raises CL 29-64 % (Davis 1988, on CPAP).

variables.label: Chest wall compliance
variables.notes: Gerhardt & Bancalari 1980: 6.4 /kg (32 wk). Very compliant chest wall: Ccw/CL ~6 here.

variables.label: Respiratory system resistance
variables.notes: Reiterer 61; Cunningham 76-94; Bhutani 106 (acute). Pneumotach values include the upper airway; nasal prongs not modelled.

variables.label: Functional residual capacity
variables.notes: da Silva 1994 (28.3 wk, 1168 g, day 3-7, after surfactant, intubated): 18.4 / 19.7 / 22.6 / 26.2 at PEEP 2/3/4/5. Nasal CPAP 6 delivers ~5.4 cmH2O at the pharynx (Liew).

variables.label: Anatomic dead space
variables.notes: User decision ~3 (term 2.2). Numa & Newth extrathoracic 2.3 + intrathoracic 1.0 = 3.3; Williams ~2.3 below the tube. Nasal CPAP does not wash out the nasopharynx (Liew), so nose-to-bronchiole dead space applies.

variables.label: Physiological dead space fraction (Vd/Vt)
variables.notes: Williams VD/VT 0.67 (ventilated incl. apparatus); Liew back-calculated physiological VD ~3.3 mL/kg.

variables.label: Inspired O2 fraction
variables.notes: State definition (nCPAP 6, FiO2 0.25), not a measured variable.

variables.label: Apnoea / periodic breathing
variables.notes: Reference only; Apnea model off at baseline. Pre-Vent (717 infants <29 wk): events start rising from day 3, peak at 3-4 weeks; periodic breathing peaks at 31-33 wk PMA. Occasional short central pauses on day 3 are optional.

variables.label: SpO2 (pre-ductal)
variables.notes: European Consensus 2022: target 90-94 %, alarms 89/95. NeOProM: 85-89 % raised mortality. AVIOx: infants <28 wk on support had median achieved 95 %. Pre- and post-ductal equal with a restrictive L->R duct.

variables.label: pH
variables.notes: Derived (Van Slyke) from BE -5.5 and pCO2 46. Bonsante 2017 (<=29 wk, ~1 kg, days 2-7): pH 7.24-7.30. European guideline tolerates pH > 7.22 while weaning.

variables.label: pCO2
variables.notes: Fabres 2007 time-weighted 47 over days 1-4 (26 wk); PHELBI control arm days 1-3 40-50; Liew TcCO2 ~49 on nCPAP 6. Requires alveolar ventilation ~105-115 mL/kg/min at VCO2 ~5.7.

variables.label: HCO3
variables.notes: Derived from pH and pCO2.

variables.label: Base excess
variables.notes: User decision -5 to -6 (modern early PN). Bonsante -5.1 / -6.4 / -8.7 across PN cohorts (more aggressive PN -> lower BE); Notz 2024: base deficit worst on day 3. Lactate explains little of it.

variables.label: PaO2
variables.notes: Quine & Stenson 2009 (<29 wk, week 1): SpO2 85 % ~ 40 mmHg, 95 % ~ 54 mmHg. Castillo 2008: median 54 at SpO2 85-93 %. Requires a fetal-Hb dissociation curve.

variables.label: Hb-O2 P50 (standard)
variables.notes: De Halleux 2002: <=27 wk week 1 untransfused P50 18.5 +/- 0.8, HbF 93 %; after transfusion 21.0. In vivo at pH 7.26 ~20-21.

variables.label: Mixed venous O2 saturation
variables.notes: Fick: Hb 14.5, systemic flow 195, VO2 6, SaO2 0.93 -> SvO2 ~77 %, O2 extraction ~0.17. Yapakci 2014 IVC sat (UVC) 64.8 % at 72 h is lower-body blood.

variables.label: Oxygen consumption
variables.notes: No day-3 CPAP+caffeine calorimetry. Bauer 1997 5.8 (<1500 g, week 1, thermoneutral); Bauer 2003 4.7 (25-28 wk, day 6, no support); caffeine +26 % (Bauer 2001); Schulze 2001 7.6 ventilated (lung ~25 %). Fits pCO2 46 with the agreed ventilation.

variables.label: Respiratory quotient
variables.notes: Bauer 2003 ~0.96; RQ > 1 on high-glucose PN (Forsyth 1992). VCO2 ~5.7 mL/kg/min.

variables.label: Core temperature
variables.notes: Sauer 1984: neutral core 36.7-37.3.

variables.label: Incubator air temperature
variables.notes: ~1 kg, day 3, RH ~70 %. Sauer table not readable; +-20 % RH shifts required air temperature by ~1.5-1.9 degC.

variables.label: Incubator relative humidity
variables.notes: 2021 review: 60-70 % in week 1 for >= 26 wk; many units start >= 80 %.

variables.label: Insensible water loss
variables.notes: J Perinatol 2025: 47.7 at 70 % RH vs 28.8 at 90 % RH (22-28 wk). Reference only.

variables.label: Plasma glucose
variables.notes: User decision: calm target below the cohort mean. Liu 2026 REACT substudy (27.4 wk, 890 g, PN): day 3 7.4 +/- 2.8, 33 % of samples > 8.

variables.label: Lactate
variables.notes: Liu 2026: day 2 1.72, day 3 1.51, day 4 1.33; day 3 without insulin 1.35 +/- 0.70. Hyperlactataemia > 2.5 (Deshpande & Platt 1997).

variables.label: Hemoglobin
variables.notes: User decision: delayed cord clamping, untransfused. Birth at 28 wk 15.8 (Jopling regression; Banerjee n=890 15.8 +/- 2.6); early fall in <29 wk; ~10 mL/kg sampled by 72 h (Puia-Dumitrescu: 30 mL/kg in week 1 at 25 wk); delayed clamping ~+1 g/dL.

variables.label: Hematocrit
variables.notes: Birth 46.4 % (Jopling); Mintzer 26-wk infants 35.2 % on day 3 after 10 mL/kg sampling (early clamping).

variables.label: Fetal haemoglobin fraction
variables.notes: De Halleux 2002: 92.9 +/- 1.1 % in <=27 wk before transfusion. Reference only (sets P50).

variables.label: Blood volume
variables.model_readout: sum of blood compartment volumes / weight
variables.notes: Aladangady RBC-label 71 +/- 12 (day 1), 74 with delayed vs 63 with early clamping; plasma-marker methods read higher (Bauer 1993 83 +/- 19).

variables.label: GFR
variables.notes: ~0.5 mL/min/kg (0.3-0.8). Vieux 2010 day-7 curve gives 11.1 at 28 wk (engine's renal reference, ~0.64 mL/min/kg); ~20 % lower on day 3 (user decision). Bueva 1994 ~0.5 mL/min/kg at day 1.5.

variables.label: Urine output
variables.notes: Day 3 sits in the diuretic phase (Lorenz 1995, <=1000 g: median 25-96 h).

variables.label: Fractional sodium excretion
variables.notes: Lorenz pre-diuretic 6.2 %, rising during diuresis. Reference only.

variables.label: Plasma creatinine
variables.notes: Miall 1999: cord 73, rises over 48 h (peak 221 at 23-26 wk). Reflects maternal creatinine. Reference only.
